I am just arrived from Melbourne this morning with a great regret not to have been in New Orleans for meeting you. But fate is blind and can offer me a very next opportunity to go to the States for another film. I suppose you have well received my letter dated November the 11th that I have sent you from Calcutta. items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: I played a melody against John Philip Sousa's, see I'm mixed up, National Angler March. Because these numbers was on the photograph. And I played along with them.

ctx.x: I wouldn't have heard of it. I've never heard of the sheet music for this particular quadrille that Tiger Rag is supposed to be taken from. But we've got sheet music for London Bridge so what does that prove? Well I'll show you how you prove it.

The bridge is falling down. Now you put the stops to it and I'll lay my head on the track of it, idiot. Because I created it. And I know where it comes from. nowhere it comes from. Now we come to the back part, the other part is the riage of the London Bridge. In other words, I could compose too, but I had a simple mind. I was, as they say, elementary. But I had more originality than all these people that live today in this music. Now we come to the last part. We play, I play a melody against John Philip Sousa's,…
